Patch Set 1:

(6 comments)

AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Some concerns, see inline comments. This now applies the PM-QoS request to up to two cpts on every successful send, including server-side AST sends, so on a busy node most of the machine ends up held at `pmqos_latency_max_usec`; it would help to state what that costs in idle residency, and whether the requester-side kick wants its own tunable rather than riding on `enable_pmqos`.

Uploaded patch set 2.

commit.subject: LU-20661 ptlrpc: Lower CPU latency system wide
commit.message:
LU-20661 ptlrpc: Lower CPU latency system wide

kick_cpu_latency() only lowered the latency of the cpt the primary
NID maps to, while the thread consuming the reply runs elsewhere
-- the caller for a sync RPC, a ptlrpcd for an async one.  Take a
single system wide cpu_latency_qos request instead of a per CPU
device DEV_PM_QOS_RESUME_LATENCY one, with a shim for kernels
before v5.7.

cpu_latency_work() also read jiffies_64 twice, so the delay it
computes could underflow, costing a spurious wakeup.  Read it
once.

Default enable_pmqos to CONFIG_CPU_IDLE and reject enabling it
when that option is off, since the PM QoS calls are then stubs.

Fixes: 54a64ea818d9 ("LU-18446 ptlrpc: lower CPUs latency during client I/O")
Signed-off-by: Xiao Yang <xyang@ddn.com>
Change-Id: Ic2e051c4f1fe78e1c55fd1d2688e15a4579567a3
